name: Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm
summary: In the Stonetalon Mountains, goblin operatives seek Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm to prove his death and clear out competition. The grafted limb belonged to rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle.

sections.title: A Bizarre Invention
sections.body: Above Cragpool Lake, rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle grafted whirring gears and metal onto his failing body. The renegade gnome replaced his natural limbs with intricate machinery. Goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks wants Gerenzo eliminated to impress his superiors. The distinctive arm is the proof he needs of the engineer's death.

sections.title: Gnomish Philosophy, Goblin Critique
sections.body: Ziz Fizziks sees little sense in cutting off a working arm for a mechanical replacement. A proper goblin engineer, he says, would keep both natural arms and mount a mechanical third one. Still, delivering the severed limb satisfies Sputtervalve. It also helps Ziz petition for an assignment in Gadgetzan or Undermine.

faq.q: Where does Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm come from?
faq.answer: Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees logging and engineering operations high above Cragpool Lake, near the water wheel in the Stonetalon Mountains. The arm comes from him.

faq.q: Why does Ziz Fizziks want this arm?
faq.answer: Ziz Fizziks needs proof for his superior, Sputtervalve, that Gerenzo is dead. Gerenzo's unique prosthetic arm cannot be forged or mistaken for anyone else's.

faq.q: Why did Gerenzo replace his own arm?
faq.answer: Ziz Fizziks says Gerenzo's flesh appeared to be rotting away. Gerenzo grafted machinery onto himself and replaced his failing limbs with mechanical counterparts, driven by desperation or obsessive gnomish experimentation.

angles.text: The arm shows two different engineering traditions. Gnomes willingly sacrifice their own biology for mechanical precision, while goblins favor external additions and brute firepower.
Gerenzo represents a grim extreme of gnomish ingenuity. He took mechanical replacement far beyond conventional medical prosthetics and into morbid self-augmentation.
